newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity mixed though little changed.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity mixed though little changed.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were trading mixed but little changed Monday in thin volume, industry sources said.

As of 1235 EDT, September Palo Verde (PV) was trading up seven cents at $30.40 per megawatt hour (MWh) following exchanges in a range of $30.10-30.60, while October was trading up 40 cents at the day's high of $23.60 after reaching as low as $23.50 per MWh.

September California Oregon Border (COB) was trading down 10 cents at the day's high of $22.80 after reaching as low as $22.75, while October was bid at $22.30 and offered at $22.50 from Friday's close at $22.30 per MWh.
NYMEX trade volumes were not available as of midday Monday, but sources said the number of exchanges was relatively thin.

In the physical markets, next-day peak PV was said to be trading at $29.00-30.25 from $26.00-27.50 for Saturday/Monday delivery, while next-day COB was said to have traded at $19.00-19.50 from $17.50-19.00 for Saturday/Monday delivery.

In Western news, the 3,800 megawatt (MW) AC segment of the Pacific Intertie was scheduled to be curtailed to 2,950 MW between 0800-1600 PDT Monday to Friday, while the DC line will be limited to 2,360 over the same period.
A high pressure ridge building in the West was expected to heat the region's temperatures three to seven degrees Fahrenheit above normal through Friday, meteorologists said.

In its latest six to 10 day forecast, Weather Services Corp said temperatures would average below normal along the coastal region, near normal further inland and above normal in the eastern part of the Southwest.
Most baseload units in the West were said to be operating at normal levels early Monday.
The 1,221 MW unit 2 at the Palo Verde generating complex in Arizona continued to coast down toward its refueling outage in September.
The unit, in Wintersburg, Ariz., was operating at 81 percent power early Monday, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission said in its daily plant status report.
COB open interest for August 15 fell four to 5,292, while PV open interest rose 53 to 5,604, NYMEX said.
